summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with quadriplegia, tracheostomy, GJ tube, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter was admitted from his nursing home for fever and elevated white blood cell count. He was found to have healthcare-associated pneumonia and a complicated urinary tract infection caused by Proteus mirabilis. He was treated with IV antibiotics, initially cefepime and linezolid, then switched to meropenem based on culture results. His GJ tube clogged on hospital day 3, requiring intervention by interventional radiology to unclog it; tube feeds and medications were resumed afterward. His warfarin was held due to a supratherapeutic INR of 5.4, likely from a drug interaction with levofloxacin, and was restarted when INR normalized. He developed transient anemia, likely dilutional, with no evidence of bleeding. Pressure ulcers were managed with wound care and repositioning. He improved clinically, became afebrile, and had normalizing labs. He was discharged to extended care with a PICC line to complete a 10-day course of IV antibiotics and instructions for ongoing wound, respiratory, and medication management.
